outcomes.text: Handle a book correctly and know English text runs left to right, top to bottom.
Match capital and small letters and tell the sounds of letters in words.
Read common sight words, naming and action words, and read words aloud with reasonable accuracy.
Predict a story from pictures, find specific facts and follow a simple procedure; say likes and dislikes about a story.
Name objects in a picture, read a calendar's month and day, and say a word or sentence about them.
Put words in alphabetical order, brainstorm ideas and find texts by title and picture.
Recite short poems with actions, listen to and read a short story, name characters and say whether they liked it.
Hold a pencil, trace and copy letters, write simple words, numbers 1-10, date, name and a copied sentence.
Write naming and action words for pictures, list similar items and fill in words to complete a story.
Make greeting cards with copied names and phrases and fill speech bubbles with given words.
Offer and answer greetings, use basic courtesies, follow commands and express limited needs.
Take turns, introduce self, express likes, recite poems and use body language.

units.title: C4 Formal and Lexical Aspects of Language

outcomes.text: Say letter sounds, match initial sounds to pictures, tell consonants from vowels and rhyming words.
Tell /s/ and /z/ plural endings, say weak forms of a and an and listen to stories for rhythm.
Use English words from home, naming and action words, colours, shapes, numbers and left/right.
Spell one- or two-syllable words, copy words and supply missing letters; use class phrases.
Use naming words, singular and plural with s, gender, particular names, and pronouns I, you, he, she, we, they, it.
Use common action words, am/is/are, describing words and possessives my, your, his, her, our, their.
Capitalise the first word of a sentence and use full stop, question mark and exclamation mark.
Use and respond to simple requests, commands and wh- questions.
Tell the sounds of letters, digraphs and trigraphs at the start and end of words.
Read more sight words and simple sentences aloud, and see that words in a sentence join to make sense.
Locate facts to answer short questions, follow simple notices and signs, and respond to a story by role play.
Say sentences about pictures, read a clock by the hour, a calendar, picture map keys and classroom charts.
Order words by first and second letter, use a table of contents and a picture dictionary.
Read and recite poems, read a story aloud, name characters and write a sentence on likes and dislikes.
Write two- or three-syllable words, numbers to 50 and ordinals, date, address, and simple sentences of 3-6 words.
Write a few sentences about pictures, list items by category and complete a story.
Write simple greeting cards and fill speech bubbles or cartoon strips with a simple dialogue.
Greet, introduce self and family, follow commands, express needs and feelings and ask permission.
Introduce self and others, use polite expressions, describe things around them and recite poems.

units.title: C4 Formal and Lexical Aspects of Language

outcomes.text: Match initial and final sounds, say digraphs and two-consonant clusters, and classify words by sound.
Tell /s/, /z/ and /iz/ plural endings, say weak forms and syllabify simple words.
Classify naming and action words, use ordinal numbers to ten and follow multi-step directions.
Spell two- or three-syllable words, take dictation and supply missing letters.
Classify naming words, make plurals with s and es, and distinguish and use pronouns and pointing words.
Use has/have, can/cannot, opposites, its, and position words such as up/down and here/there.
Capitalise names of people, pets and places, end sentences correctly, and use commas in lists and after Yes and No.
Use and respond to requests, commands and wh- questions in speech.
Read words with digraphs, trigraphs and inflections; see how sentences join into a paragraph using pronouns and transitions.
Predict from title and picture, find facts, infer missing words, follow public signs, and respond to a text using own experience.
Describe events in a picture, read a picture map, a clock by half hour, a timetable and picture graphs.
Use alphabetical order, textual aids such as contents pages and simple keys on maps.
Recite poems with actions, find characters in a story and retell it in a few sentences.
Spell multi-syllable words, write numbers to 100 and ordinals to thirtieth, and write sentences and a short paragraph on a topic.
List vocabulary for a task, complete a paragraph and write simple descriptive, narrative and process paragraphs.
Write guided short notes and informal invitations, and sentences in speech bubbles.
Revise written work for layout, legibility and punctuation.
Use formulaic expressions for greetings, gratitude, regret, opinions, needs and instructions suited to the listener.
Greet, introduce, converse, take turns, agree and disagree politely, lead and follow, with suitable tone and non-verbal cues.

units.title: C4 Formal and Lexical Aspects of Language

outcomes.text: Say hard and soft c and g, silent letters, long and short vowels, two-consonant clusters, ed endings and syllables, and rising and falling intonation.
Use cognates, anagrams, rhyming words, word classes, synonyms and antonyms.
Organise words alphabetically and by part of speech, spell class words and apply plural spelling changes.
Use countable and uncountable, common and proper nouns, plurals and gender; pronouns and their agreement; articles a and an.
Use be, do, have, can and may, and simple present, present continuous and simple past tenses.
Use adjectives of quantity, quality, size and colour, position words, and and, or, but, because.
Capitalise days and months; use apostrophe for possession and exclamation mark.
Make SV and SVO sentences, subject-verb agreement, commands, exclamations and wh- questions.
Read words with silent letters, compounds and inflections; link sentences with transitional devices and see paragraphs as units of thought.
Guess word meaning from context, tell fact from opinion, follow maps and notices, and summarise with a mind map.
Describe a series of events, read maps, clocks, timetables, pie charts and bar graphs.
Use a dictionary, note-taking, glossary and contents, and read keys on maps and tables in textbooks.
Recite poems, tell when and where a story is set, describe characters, express preferences and retell sequentially.
Gather and organise ideas with brainstorming and mind maps and write a unified paragraph with a topic sentence and conjunctions.
Write descriptive, narrative and expository paragraphs, a guided story with story elements, and a central idea of a poem.
Write short notes, informal invitations with date, time and venue, replies, and an informal letter with its conventions.
Revise for spelling, punctuation, pronoun and subject-verb agreement, vocabulary and grammar.
Express regret, likes and dislikes, needs, opinions, permission and ability.
Introduce others, converse, make polite requests, take leave and use suitable tone and non-verbal cues.

units.title: C4 Formal and Lexical Aspects of Language

outcomes.text: Say more silent letters, three-consonant clusters, weak forms and mark rising and falling tones.
Change parts of speech, use homophones, compound words, similes and common verb collocations.
Organise words by part of speech and word family, find dictionary entries and spell irregular plurals.
Use collective nouns, irregular plurals, possessive pronouns, pointing and question words; a, an and mute consonants.
Use helping verbs, should, irregular verbs, past continuous and simple future tense.
Use adjectives by type with degrees, adverbs of manner and time, prepositions and sequence words.
Capitalise holidays and events; use full stops in abbreviations, apostrophe in contractions, hyphen and colon.
Make SV and SVO sentences, agreement, commands, statements, negatives and wh- questions.
Syllabify words with silent letters and affixes; find the topic sentence of a paragraph and relate sentences and paragraphs.
Scan for information, make simple inferences, comprehend factual, interpretive and inferential questions, and summarise with a mind map.
Describe a sequence in a diagram, read maps, report cards and compare pie chart with bar graph.
Use a dictionary, mind maps, note-taking and glossary, and read tables and charts in textbooks.
Describe story elements giving reasons for preferences, retell sequentially and summarise a folktale.
Analyse paragraph structure and write a guided paragraph with topic sentence, support and conjunctions within and between paragraphs.
Tell descriptive, narrative and expository paragraphs apart, describe from general to specific, write stories with dialogue and short fables.
Write notes, invitations and replies that accept or decline, and speech-bubble text in suitable tone.
Revise for spelling, punctuation, agreement, layout, vocabulary and grammar.
Express and respond to opinions, offer and accept apology, make requests and give instructions.
Introduce others, converse, take turns, lead and follow, express needs, feelings and ideas with suitable tone.

units.title: C4 Formal and Lexical Aspects of Language

outcomes.text: Say silent-letter patterns, consonant clusters, vowel sounds, weak forms and respond to rising and falling intonation.
Change parts of speech, use homophones and homonyms, compounds, analogies and collocations.
Organise words by part of speech and word family, find dictionary entries and spell irregular nouns and verbs.
Use reflexive pronouns, my-mine pairs, gender of nouns, question words and the definite article.
Use be, do, have as main or helping verbs, modals for permission and obligation, and four basic tenses.
Use degrees of irregular adjectives, adverbs of manner, time, place and frequency, prepositions of direction and linking phrases.
Capitalise key words in titles; use hyphen with numbers and fractions.
Use SVO with direct and indirect objects, agreement, commands and wh- questions.
Analyse a paragraph for its topic sentence and supporting details, and see how paragraphs build one theme.
Judge how specific words, vivid verbs and modifiers make a strong topic sentence, and how definition, example and evidence support it.
Use pronoun-antecedent links, transitional devices and the order of paragraph details (chronological, spatial, importance) for coherence.

Ask and answer questions, request, seek permission, give directions, and express reasons for likes and needs.
Take part in group discussion: greet, compliment, invite, take turns, lead and follow, agree and disagree politely.
